solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rock is what starts party best

indicators.note: what starts a word is its opening letter, so only the head of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of party
the elite are the best of a group

explanation.surface: A rock fan claims that the best thing about a party is the music at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' reads as music in the surface, but it is a geological definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelite is a sedimentary rock made of fine clay or mud particles, a geologist's term found in Chambers.

clue.text: Part of bridge end nicked? That's criminal

indicators.note: something nicked has been stolen away, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: a perpend is a bond stone running right through a wall, as in a bridge's masonry
taken as written; these are the letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone has pinched the end of a bridge, which is clearly a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicked' suggests theft for the surface and also for the definition, but here it removes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Perp is American police slang, short for perpetrator, the person who committed a crime.

clue.text: Having no heart for crowd in jostling queues, I'd avoid the Army and Navy

definitions.text: I'd avoid the Army and Navy

indicators.note: being in a crowd puts something inside it, so these letters go within the others
people jostling push each other about, so these letters are shoved out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: with no heart the middle is cut away, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: a mob is a crowd

explanation.surface: Someone who hates crowds and jostling queues says they would steer clear of the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The first-person definition is spoken by the shirker: an embusqué is someone who has dodged service with the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: An embusqué is a person who dodges military service, often by taking a safe job away from the front.

clue.text: Unwound on cruise? Naturally for veterans

indicators.note: something unwound has come loose from its coil, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: the two words taken together

explanation.surface: Old soldiers relax on a cruise as they naturally would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for veterans' marks an old-fashioned phrase, not real servicemen.
explanation.definitionFit: In course is an archaic phrase meaning of course, in the natural order of things, which old speakers would use.

clue.text: Hope IT working for old African

indicators.note: working means in motion and busy, so these letters are set moving into a new order

parts.note: the two words taken together

explanation.surface: An elderly African man hopes the computer system is working.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethiop is an archaic word for an Ethiopian or, more broadly, a Black African.

clue.text: Fish weight brought back for fair

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: the dab is a small flatfish
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's catch is weighed and returned as a fair deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not bad is a mild British way of calling it fair or reasonably good.

clue.text: Theatrical Lionel gets work with lead perhaps

indicators.note: a theatrical act puts on a show and plays a part, so these letters take on a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor called Lionel lands a job playing a lead role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a starring role but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Niello is a black alloy of sulphur with silver, copper and lead, used to fill engraved metalwork, and the decorative work made with it.

clue.text: Bajan's small heap (not a Tesla) inclined to shake in the Highlands

definitions.text: inclined to shake in the Highlands

indicators.note: not having something means going without it, so this letter is struck out

parts.note: a bajan is a first-year student at Aberdeen, so this is the Scots word for a small heap or tuft
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density; a means one of them

explanation.surface: A small pile from Barbados that is not an electric car seems to be trembling in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Bajan looks like a Barbadian, but in Scots it is a first-year Aberdeen student, which flags a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oorie is Scots for dismal or chilly, and so shivering or apt to shudder with cold.

clue.text: Two containers, one in a poor state

wordplay.note: a basket and a case are both containers

explanation.surface: A pair of boxes, one of them in bad repair.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket case is informal for a person or thing in a hopeless or helpless condition.

clue.text: Nanny not drinking before noon, sure to be relaxed

indicators.note: something relaxed has loosened its hold, so these letters fall out of order
one thing coming before another fixes the order, so the first piece leads

parts.note: someone dry is not drinking alcohol
N is the abbreviation for noon
the word rearranged

explanation.surface: A nanny who abstains until midday is sure to be calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry nurse looks after a baby without breastfeeding it, which is what a nanny does.

clue.text: Effusive in public after getting English degree

indicators.note: one thing coming after another sets the order, so the later word's letters follow the earlier ones

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
an MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree
national, as in a national institution, means belonging to the public at large

explanation.surface: Someone gushes openly in public after earning a degree in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Effusive' looks like a description of a gushing graduate, but it is the definition in its literal sense of flowing out.
explanation.definitionFit: Emanational means relating to emanation, the flowing out or issuing forth of something, which is the root sense of effusive.

clue.text: Old star has the desired effect, making duff parts

parts.note: stern is an obsolete word for a star
a plan that works has the effect wanted

explanation.surface: A faded celebrity still succeeds, despite turning out shoddy spare parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duff' reads as useless, but it is slang for the backside, so duff parts are the rear parts of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternworks are the structures at the back of a ship, and duff is slang for the rear or bottom.

clue.text: Esther lost in outskirts of county town

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one set of letters goes within the other
something lost has wandered off its proper path, so these letters stray out of order

parts.note: the name rearranged

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of county

explanation.surface: A woman called Esther has got lost on the edge of a county town.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled name sits between C and Y. Chertsey is a town in Surrey, south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Chertsey is a market town in the English county of Surrey, on the River Thames.

clue.text: Hoax in bed recalled

indicators.note: recalling something calls it back, so the letters return in the opposite direction

parts.note: someone in bed is not up yet

explanation.surface: A prank is remembered from someone's time lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bed' must be rephrased as a two-word phrase before turning it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A put-on is a deception or trick played on someone, a synonym for a hoax.

clue.text: Right to take book home once

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so one set of letters is placed within the other

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
BK is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Someone asserts a right to take a library book home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like a political or moral entitlement but is the legal term for a claim on property. 'once' marks an old word.
explanation.definitionFit: Libken is old thieves' slang for a lodging or house, so it is an archaic word for a place to live.

clue.text: False membership fees reversed in Post Office

indicators.note: sitting in something places it inside, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office

indicators.note: reversed means turned to face the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: dues are the regular fees paid by members of a club

explanation.surface: A club's fees were wrongly refunded at the Post Office.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseudo is used as an adjective meaning sham or not genuine, so it is a synonym for false.

clue.text: Engaging lawyer, go after Trinidad estate for unduly rigorous formality

indicators.note: one thing coming after another fixes the order, so this piece comes last
engaging something means taking it in and holding it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: in the Caribbean a pen is a farm or estate
a DA is a district attorney, a US prosecuting lawyer
having a go at something is a try

explanation.surface: A Caribbean estate hires a lawyer for its stiff ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaging' looks like hiring a lawyer, but it is the signal to put one piece inside another. Pen for an estate or farm is West Indian usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive attention to rules and fine detail, an overly strict insistence on correct form.

clue.text: Plant found readily around Thailand?

indicators.note: to found metal is to melt and cast it, so these letters are melted down and recast

parts.note: taken as written
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: A plant that grows easily all over Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like discovered, but here it means cast metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dielytra is an older genus name for the bleeding heart and related flowering plants, now usually called Dicentra.

clue.text: Passing over the purpose of Chambers!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: giving up or doing without
second meaning, split in two: chamber pots are there for one particular use

explanation.walkthrough: Chambers looks like the crossword dictionary, but it is chamber pots, and the answer read as two words says what they are for.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgoing means giving something up or passing it by, while split in two it states what a chamber pot is used for.

clue.text: It helps replace part of body in posterior? Not normally

definitions.text: It helps replace part of body

indicators.note: something done not normally is out of its usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: all nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical tool for putting something back in the backside, used only in unusual cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posterior' sits right next to the body-part definition, so it reads as the place; it is the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A repositor is a surgical instrument for returning a displaced organ or bone to its proper position.

clue.text: Dead wobbly straw hat

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead
something wobbly is unstable

explanation.surface: A dead man's straw hat sits wobbling on his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Dunstable, a Bedfordshire town, was a centre of straw plaiting and gave its name to a straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunstable is a hat made of plaited straw, named after the English town where such straw work was made.

clue.text: Fish feast traditionally ending with wine

indicators.note: ending with something places that piece at the close, so it follows the first

parts.note: an ale was once a village festival, as in church-ale
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A traditional fish supper finishes with a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traditionally' marks the old sense of the beer word as a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: An alevin is a young fish, especially a salmon or trout just hatched and still carrying its yolk sac.

clue.text: Snipe coming from dhak tree out of area north of North Dakota

indicators.note: in a down entry being north of something means sitting above it, so this piece comes first
taking a letter out of a word leaves it removed, so this letter is dropped

parts.note: Butea is the genus of the dhak, an Indian flowering tree
A is the abbreviation for area
ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota

explanation.surface: A wading bird emerges from an Indian tree north of an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snipe' reads as the bird, but it is slang for a cigarette end. BUTEND is Chambers' spelling of butt end.
explanation.definitionFit: A snipe is slang for a discarded cigarette end, which is the stub or remaining tail of the smoke.

clue.text: Duke with very small amount in ancient vase

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
an iota is a tiny quantity

explanation.surface: A duke keeps a tiny amount of something in an antique vase.
explanation.definitionFit: A diota is a two-handled jar or amphora of ancient Greece and Rome.

clue.text: What dreadful lager contains is the dregs

indicators.note: what a phrase contains is held inside it, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Bad beer is nothing more than sediment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' points at the letters held inside the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ullage is the amount by which a cask falls short of full, and also the sediment or dregs left in it.

clue.text: Secluded recess that's made for it!

parts.note: a nook is a secluded corner or recess
i.e., Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A hidden alcove seems purpose-built for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is slang for sex, and the exclamation mark flags the cheeky reading of a secluded spot made for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nookie is informal slang for sexual activity, which 'it' also means in coy colloquial use.

clue.text: Girl's going around as a techie

indicators.note: going around turns a thing to face the other way, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: Posy is a girl's name, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A young woman is circulating at work as the IT person.
explanation.definitionFit: A sysop is a system operator, the technician who runs a computer system or bulletin board.

clue.text: Lacking energy, lacking energy, lacking energy

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter named next is removed

parts.note: a variant spelling of an adjective meaning slow or sluggish
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Three times over, someone has no energy at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase does three jobs: one spelling of the answer, an instruction to drop E, and the definition of the shorter spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Poky means slow and sluggish, without drive, as in a poky car that will not get up a hill.

clue.text: Sales aptly shown in a pie chart?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the total amount of business a company does
second meaning: a pastry folded over a filling

explanation.surface: A business presents its sales figures in a pie chart.
explanation.walkthrough: The pie chart is a real way to show sales, but 'a pie' is also the pastry sense of the answer, which is why it is 'aptly' shown there.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnover means a firm's total revenue, and an apple turnover is a folded pastry pie.

clue.text: 500 out taking drinks to party? It must have enough ice to go round

definitions.text: It must have enough ice to go round

indicators.note: letters off to party let loose and mix about, ending up in a new order
out means removed, so this letter is struck from the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Someone takes drinks to a party and needs enough ice for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enough ice to go round' sounds like ice for the drinks, but means a frozen surface for skaters to circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A skating rink is an ice surface that skaters circle, so it needs plenty of ice to go round on.

clue.text: Negative about accommodating leaders in every single meeting? Not me

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so one set of letters is housed inside the other
about means turned around, so the word before it runs backwards

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the first letters of every, single and meeting

explanation.surface: A dissenter insists they are not the one always saying no in meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is spoken by the person who is always negative, who would never be a yes man.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes man always agrees with his superiors, the opposite of a negative speaker, so the speaker says it is not them.

clue.text: Tedious hardline Tory defending a government repeatedly

indicators.note: defending something means surrounding and guarding it, so these letters go around the others

parts.note: a dry is a hardline right-wing Conservative, a term from the Thatcher years
A, then G for government twice

explanation.surface: A dull right-wing politician keeps standing up for the government.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics a dry is a hardline Conservative, the opposite of a wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Draggy is informal for slow and dull, describing something that drags on and is tedious.
